messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Passing data between shiny apps
messages.body_plain:
If it's just a matter of passing a few hundred bytes of data, then I'd use querystring parameters, not cookies. Cookies are passed as HTTP headers which currently are stripped by Shiny Server/ShinyApps for security reasons. It's certainly possible we'd support cookies in the future, but for what you're talking about I think querystring parameters are more appropriate anyway, as they would allow back/forward navigation to work properly.

To access querystring parameters from Shiny, include a "session" parameter in your shinyServer function, i.e. function(input, output, session). Then call parseQueryString(session$clientData$url_search) which will return key-value pairs.

messages.body_plain:
ShinyApps will allow writes to occur to the filesystem, the only issue (and we think it is a significant one) is that if the server goes down, you would lose the data that is was previously written.  We are thinking about whether we should try and support a model of providing a simple data store that a developer could use on to store end-user information, or whether app creators would rather use their own datastores whether it is Amazon RDS, some other cloud hosted MySQLor Postgres, Amazon's Dynamo, Cloudant or some other hosted DB offering.

Would love to hear people's thoughts on this.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shinyapps is completely stupid
messages.body_plain:
Gunter,
Apologies that you have found ShinyApps so difficult to use.  The Platform as a service (PaaS) model is admittedly a newer paradigm that is not as well known in the industry yet.  If you are familiar with platforms like Heroku or CloudBees you can see other examples that compare to ShinyApps.  In the PaaS model, the service provider is taking care of providing you with self-contained computational resources based on your needs.   The developer can scale the resources up and down without needing to know about where the servers are hosted, how the code will be deployed and rolled out across the cluster etc...

Using an R package with semantics that are more familiar to R developers has made it easy for several hundred R developers to build an app and get it deployed within a short period of time.  It is different than a classic web hosting model, but we are hoping to learn through the alpha whether that is true or not.

If you would like to discuss this further, please don't hesitate to drop me a line.   We are using the alpha period to help us learn about what works and what doesn't and truly appreciate your feedback.

Best,
Tareef
